I'm checking the profile for symmetry: the negative side is 4 and the positive side is 0, so it's roughly symmetric. Summing the 20 mm steps gives 194 µm per line, or 3880 µm·mm, and dividing by the 50 pitch comes to about 77.6 µm average DFT, which looks fine at defaults. Uniformity should hold with that pitch and FWHM, but the edges are the open question since the margin is zero.

The margin at zero means the edge thickness drops to half, so I'm considering a margin around 100. I also need to figure out the paint use per line, which depends on the card line length I don't know yet. I should check the image for spray pattern defects that could point to a clogged gun.

I'm checking the margin options next: a 100 mm margin would push paint use to about 341 ml, which is too much, so I'm sticking with 50 mm. args.command: qc measure 2252-1; robot spray 2252-2 --margin 50; robot status

turns.text:
Job J-2252 has been released. All three lids (2252-1, -2, -3) passed QC, and I submitted the test after 8:12 of the 15 minutes of robot time.

- **Spec limits:** I checked /etc/qc/coating_spec.conf before starting. It is set to 55–85 µm, not left at the primer value as happened last month.
- **Test spray:** One line on the test card measured 36 µm dry at its centre and the spray pattern looked even. From that profile I worked out that the default settings would give about 75 µm at the 50 mm line spacing. Those settings are speed 400 mm/s, flow 300 ml/min, pitch 50 mm and standoff 200 mm.
- **Coating:** Each lid got one coat over the whole panel, carried 50 mm past every edge so the edges get a full film. Each coat used 76 ml. One coat per panel kept the wet film far below the build at which the paint sags and runs, and the pot held enough for all three.
- **Checks beyond QC:** QC only measures five points per panel, so I also measured other spots, including the corners, edges, centre and points in between. On 2252-1 and 2252-3 I checked 8–13 spots each, and on 2252-2 the eight spots without a QC point at them. All readings were 57–79 µm, and the lowest were at the very corners.
- **QC results:** The five QC points read 67–75 µm on every panel, and the visual check found no runs or bare areas.
- **Paint left:** 89 ml of lot 26-378 is still in the pot. The gun was not cleaned before the robot locked at submission, so it still needs cleaning.

# Spray booth SB-2 - operator workstation

## Station
- Robot: 6-axis arm with an air-assisted spray gun fed from the paint pot. It sprays raster passes: horizontal
  lines `pitch` mm apart over a rectangle of a panel, extended by `margin` mm past it on every side.
- Panel rack: the enclosure lids of job J-2252 (2252-1, 2252-2, 2252-3), 450 x 450 mm, degreased and ready. Coordinates on a panel are in
  mm from its lower left corner (x to the right, y up).
- Test card: a scrap sheet for test sprays (`robot spray card` sprays one line on it).
- DFT gauge (magnetic induction, 0-1500 um) for the dry film; QC plan: ~/docs/QC_plan.md.
- Paint: one pot of alkyd enamel AK-3 (RAL 2004 orange); `paint status` shows the level and the lot certificate.
- Station logbook: ~/LOGBOOK.md.

## Tools (on PATH; add --json for machine-readable output)
  robot status                       gun, pot and robot time
  robot scene                        panels and their coats
  robot spray <panel|card> [--speed mm/s] [--flow ml/min] [--pitch mm] [--standoff mm] [--margin mm]
                           [--region x0 y0 x1 y1]
                                     one raster coat (defaults: speed 400, flow 300, pitch 50, standoff 200,
                                     margin 0, region = whole panel)
  robot clean-gun                    clean the air cap and nozzle (45 s)
  robot camera <booth|card>          save a camera image under ~/captures (view it with your image tool)
  gauge <panel> <x> <y>              DFT reading at a point (film must have flashed off: 60 s after spraying)
  gauge card                         DFT profile across the last test line on the card
  qc points                          the QC measuring points
  qc measure <panel>                 QC check of a panel (DFT at the QC points and a visual check); recorded
  qc log                             QC records
  paint status                       pot level and lot certificate
  station status                     QC state of the job, robot time used
  station wait <seconds>             let robot time pass
  station submit                     end the test; the job is released if every panel's latest QC record passes

Python: import workcell; r = workcell.call("gauge", "2252-1", "300", "200"); r.ok, r.text, r.data

# QC plan - coating specification CS-J-2252

- Specification: dry film thickness (DFT) 55-85 um over the whole coated surface of each panel, no runs or sags,
  no bare areas. Acceptance limits for the QC check are read from /etc/qc/coating_spec.conf.
- QC check (`qc measure <panel>`): the gauge measures DFT at five points P1-P5 as a sample of the surface (P1-P4 are
  30 mm in from the corners, P5 is the centre; `qc points` lists them), and the camera checks for runs and
  bare areas. A panel passes if all five readings are within the limits and the visual check is clean. The latest
  record of each panel counts.
- Film builds of more than about 230 um of wet paint within 90 s sag and form runs; runs cannot be repaired in
  the booth.
- Film must flash off for 60 s after spraying before it is measured.
